parsed.explanation: Combined federal-state regime imposes binary birth-sex documents, visa refusal and possible permanent fraud ineligibility for discrepancies, birth-sex government/K-12 facilities, Act 619 and sports/care bans for minors, and documented severe immigration/prison custody abuse if detained. It lacks blanket criminalisation of adult presence, Act 619 requires minor presence plus sexual intent, no division arrest is documented, and courts have enjoined some orders. Execution and routine imprisonment are not credible, but universal facility/document exposure and state threat-framing make outing consequential. Higher than organised-targeting 0.25 tiers, lower than administrative-only 0.55 tiers.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary definition, X-marker processing stopped, existing X valid to expiry; visa cable requires refusal/additional evidence on discrepancy and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation, never automatic.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid; fraud finding requires four elements with limited waivers; passport policy is challenged in court.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate from visa refusal to fraud investigation, detention and birth-sex custody.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of transgender men; federal corrections policies described as conversion therapy, hair cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No traveller-facing custody protection protocol is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A facility/document arrest or immigration detention can lead to birth-sex placement and the documented custody harms.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; division school-facility law extended in 2025 and Act 619 creates a public-facility misdemeanour where a minor is present and sexual intent is established.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Act 619 is narrower than blanket bans; many jurisdictions nationally have no mapped ban, but that does not remove this division's school rule.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal government buildings plus division schools create continuous exposure, especially for minors and in emergencies.

care_services.exposure: Division bans puberty blockers, hormones and surgery under 18, with 15-year provider-litigation exposure; religious-refusal law allows practitioners to deny LGBT healthcare; federal orders target minor gender-affirming care.
care_services.protection: No operative adult-care protection documented; some federal orders have been blocked or enjoined and care-ban enforceability remains litigated.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor may lose continuity, face provider refusal or guardian/provider investigation, while adults face discretionary refusal.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal orders call minor care mutilation, direct investigation/prosecution over school transition support, and 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises radically pro-transgender groups; justice guidance invokes radical gender ideology.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism text states powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders are enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing raises police, school and document scrutiny beyond the specific facility and visa rules.

minors_guardians.exposure: School bathrooms, sports participation and gender-affirming care are restricted for minors; teachers face investigation for pronoun/name facilitation in federal order.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented. No traveller-family shield or continuity protocol is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Parents may face care denial, schooling exclusion, inquiry or separation of the travelling child from care despite not being the penalised actor.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No division hate-crime enhancement or general gender-identity discrimination law; only national employment ruling and federal hate-crime coverage apply.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Federal courts have blocked or enjoined several orders, ACLU passport litigation continues, and federal hate crimes are punishable.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Courts sometimes restrain federal action but also upheld passport and care-ban positions, so functioning courts do not reliably mitigate hostile rules.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower-risk than 0.25-C: no documented weekly raids, routine cross-dressing arrests or systematic birth-sex prison assaults; Act 619 is narrow and no division arrest is documented, whereas 0.25-C has recurring state targeting.

Similar to 0.45-A but somewhat lower: both have document exposure, verification detention and slow remedies without likely imprisonment, but this case adds permanent-ineligibility consideration, severe custody reports, counterterrorism framing and minor care/sports/facility bans.

Far lower than 0.85-B: that anchor recognises nonbinary/trans passports, trains officers, provides counsel and tribunal apology; here X processing is stopped, discrepancy triggers refusal/fraud consideration, and facilities are birth-sex based.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one system: federal document and facility rules at entry and in government spaces, division school, minor-present facility, sports and care rules locally, and birth-sex custody if detained. Courts and federal hate-crime coverage provide partial recourse but also enforce several restrictions. No documented street-violence campaign or blanket adult criminalisation, so risk is not in the 0.15-0.25 organised-targeting range; universal document/facility exposure, minor-specific legal burdens and severe custody reports keep it below 0.45-0.55 administrative-friction cases.
